data.why: MicroGrowth ships its own Excel example growth-curve data and plate maps (wide and long format) that match the upload schema the app validates for (Time + well columns; rows + 1-12 plate map).

goals: Upload raw plate-reader OD time-series data and a plate map, and validate that wells map correctly to strains/conditions/replicates
Baseline-correct OD readings using blank wells and compute maximum OD, maximum specific growth rate (mu_max), lag time, and exponential phase boundaries for each well
Compare non-parametric (sliding window, spline) and parametric (logistic, Gompertz, Richards, Baranyi-Roberts) growth models to see which fits the data best
Quality-control individual well fits interactively (lasso-select outliers, adjust phase boundaries, mark wells as no-growth) before trusting the results
Visualize results across the whole 96-well plate and compare growth metrics across experimental groups/replicates
Export curated growth statistics and publication-ready plots as a packaged download

review.summary: The tree follows MicroGrowth's stated workflow closely: upload a plate and its map, set blank correction, fit spline or parametric models, check fits well by well, compare groups, and export a ZIP. The cited screens mostly show what the nodes say. Before filing, it needs the fit-quality outline colours corrected, the blank-group bug claim withdrawn, preprocessing and no-growth thresholds added, and the oversized plate-overview feature split.
